source.title: Intriguing Properties of Adversarial Examples
source.authors: E. Cubuk; Barret Zoph; S. Schoenholz; Quoc V. Le

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: Reports a fully connected network trained on randomly shuffled MNIST labels reaching perfect training accuracy, bearing on V1's random-label training-error claim. It does not test the broader CIFAR convolutional-network recipe.
record.gate_note: Other adversarial-error and accuracy results do not measure training classification error. The perfect-accuracy result is explicitly stated in the text; no numerical accuracy value is given.
record.test_reason: The shuffled-label experiment uses memorization to test whether adversarial-error scaling depends on generalization. Its fully connected MNIST network does not test V1's claim about convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100. No results test V2–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately describes the shuffled-label experiment: adversarial-error scaling persists despite the lack of generalization. The paper's broader conclusion is that logit differences and adversarial error exhibit universal scaling, and architecture affects adversarial robustness, which correlates strongly with clean accuracy.
record.recipe_differences: The reported experiment is fully connected MNIST training with shuffled labels; it does not report the CIFAR convolutional-network recipes in V1.

fits_no_version.finding: A fully connected network trained on MNIST with shuffled labels reaches perfect training accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fully connected networks can memorize shuffled MNIST training labels.

record.problems: For the training-accuracy result, the text gives no numerical accuracy, model size, optimizer, initialization details, or uncertainty.
record.rows_left_out: Adversarial-error measurements, clean test accuracies, and architecture-search results do not measure training classification error, so they were not included as rows.

untested.parts: Training classification error of convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100, including random labels and the stated optimizer, initialization, size, stopping, and regularization conditions.
Teacher-student ReLU optimization, spurious local minima, and the effect of extra student neurons.
Depth-dependent training degradation and its prevention through shortcuts or special initialization.
Effects of initialization on training speed and trainable depth.
Training loss and curvature dynamics around learning-rate stability thresholds.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and the Fixup comparison.

record.verdict_notes: Perfect accuracy establishes zero training classification error in the reported MNIST experiment. The exclusion concerns the scope of the supplied versions, not the validity of that observation. Optimizer and initialization are unspecified.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100; sufficiently large convolutional networks; SGD or Adam; smaller models, early stopping, and regularized recipes.

rows.subject: fully connected network
rows.operation_detail: Trained on MNIST with shuffled labels until perfect training accuracy.
rows.locator: Section 2, paragraph beginning “Next, we probe the relationship between generalization and adversarial robustness”
rows.note: The text reports perfect training accuracy but gives no percentage or other numerical value.
rows.check: Perfect training accuracy is explicitly reported and is a valid observation, but the fully connected MNIST experiment falls outside V1's specified architecture and datasets. It cannot establish the stated V1 effect; remove its V1 link.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
